1.g3 d5 2.Bg2 e5 3.c4.strategy: Hits the d5-pawn with a pawn backed by the bishop on g2, so d5 is attacked twice and defended only by the queen. It is the principled way to challenge Black's centre, but if Black takes, White has given a pawn and needs open lines as compensation.

1.g3 d5 2.Bg2 e5 3.b4.strategy: Throws the b-pawn forward at once: ...Bxb4 wins it, and nothing attacks the bishop on b4. The fianchettoed bishop is blocked by the d5-pawn, so White has no pressure to show for the pawn and Black can simply develop.
1.g3 d5 2.Bg2 e5 3.b4.name: Hungarian Opening: Bücker Gambit

1.g3 d5 2.Bg2 e5 3.c4 dxc4.strategy: Takes the pawn and, by removing the d5-pawn, lets the bishop on g2 aim straight at b7. Black is a pawn up and has to decide whether to hold it or give it back to finish development in peace.
